en: creator; author of an original work

examples.ko: 이 웹툰의 창작자는 아직 스무 살이에요.
examples.en: The creator of this webtoon is still twenty years old.

examples.ko: 창작자와 직접 이야기할 수 있는 행사가 있어요.
examples.en: There is an event where you can talk directly with the creator.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 창작자가 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I have wanted to become a creator since I was little.

examples.ko: 좋은 창작자는 매일 조금씩 작품을 만들어요.
examples.en: A good creator makes a little work every day.

examples.ko: 창작자의 허락 없이 그림을 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not use a drawing without the creator's permission.
There are so many young creators on the internet.

explain: 창작자는 만든 사람 중에서도 처음부터 새로 만든 사람을 가리켜요. 그림, 노래, 글처럼 작품을 만드는 사람에게 쓰고, 공장에서 물건을 만드는 사람에게는 '제작자'나 '생산자'를 써요. 요즘은 유튜브나 웹툰에서 활동하는 사람을 말할 때 자주 들려요.
explain_en: 창작자 is someone who makes an original work from scratch, like a drawing, song, or story. For people who produce goods in a factory, Koreans say 제작자 or 생산자 instead. You hear it a lot now for people active on YouTube or in webtoons.

examples.en: The student council is preparing the festival this week.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 총학생회 회장을 뽑는 날이에요.
examples.en: Today is the day we choose the president of our school's student council.
The student council handed out snacks to the students.

examples.ko: 형은 대학교 때 총학생회 활동을 했어요.
examples.en: My older brother was active in the student council in college.
The student council held a meeting about the tuition issue.
If you have questions, ask at the student council office.

explain: 총학생회는 대학교 전체 학생을 대표하는 모임이에요. 한 학과나 한 반을 대표하는 '학생회'보다 범위가 커서 앞에 '총'이 붙어요. 대학생들은 줄여서 '총학'이라고 많이 불러요.
explain_en: 총학생회 represents all the students of a university. It is bigger than a 학생회, which covers one department or class, so it gets the prefix 총. University students often shorten it to 총학.

examples.ko: 저는 고고학에 관심이 있어서 박물관에 자주 가요.
examples.en: I'm interested in archaeology, so I go to museums often.

examples.ko: 고고학을 공부하면 옛날 사람들의 생활을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you study archaeology, you can learn how people lived long ago.
My uncle teaches archaeology at a university.
The archaeology research team found a new tomb.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 고고학자가 되는 게 꿈이었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my dream was to become an archaeologist.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 고고학 이야기라서 정말 재미있어요.
examples.en: This movie is about archaeology, so it's really fun.

explain: 고고학은 땅속에서 나온 물건으로 옛날 생활을 알아보는 공부예요. 옛날 기록을 읽어서 과거를 연구하는 '역사학'과 달라요. 사람은 '고고학자'라고 불러요.
explain_en: 고고학 studies how people lived through objects dug out of the ground. It differs from 역사학, which studies the past by reading old records. A person in this field is a 고고학자.

en: to act silly; to fool around

examples.en: My little brother keeps fooling around and it's chaotic.
You must not act silly in front of the teacher.
I was fooling around too much and broke a cup.
Stop messing around and sit quietly!

examples.ko: 우리 강아지는 산책할 때 제일 많이 까불어요.
examples.en: My puppy acts the silliest when we go for walks.

examples.ko: 형이 아직도 애처럼 까부는 게 웃겨요.
examples.en: It's funny that my brother still acts like a kid.

explain: 까불다는 가볍고 시끄럽게 장난치는 모습이에요. 아이나 강아지에게는 귀엽게 들리지만 어른에게 '까불지 마'라고 하면 건방지다는 경고라서 아주 세게 들려요. ㄹ이 빠져서 '까부는, 까부세요'처럼 활용해요.
explain_en: 까불다 describes noisy, light-hearted messing around. It sounds cute for a child or puppy, but telling an adult 까불지 마 is a harsh warning meaning "don't get cocky." The ㄹ drops before some endings, as in 까부는 and 까부세요.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 모두 단합해서 일을 끝냈어요.
examples.en: Our whole team pulled together and finished the work.

examples.ko: 회사 사람들이 단합하려고 같이 등산을 갔어요.
examples.en: The coworkers went hiking together to build unity.

examples.ko: 반 친구들이 단합하면 이길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the classmates unite, we can win.
The sight of the players pulling together was really cool.

examples.ko: 다 같이 단합했기 때문에 행사가 성공했어요.
examples.en: The event succeeded because everyone pulled together.
I believe we will pull together.

explain: 단합하다는 여러 사람이 한마음으로 힘을 모으는 거예요. 비슷한 '협력하다'는 일을 같이 하는 것이고, 단합하다는 마음이 하나가 되는 쪽이에요. 회사 행사에서 '단합 대회', '단합 모임'이라는 말을 자주 써요.
explain_en: 단합하다 is about people becoming one in spirit and putting their strength together. 협력하다 is about working on something together, while 단합하다 leans toward unity of heart. Companies often hold a 단합 대회 or 단합 모임 as a team-building event.

examples.ko: 수학 시간에 여러 가지 도형을 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned about various shapes in math class.
The child is making shapes out of colored paper.
How do I find the area of this shape?
Circles and squares are the easiest shapes.

examples.ko: 칠판에 그린 도형이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: I can't see the shape drawn on the board well.

examples.ko: 발표 자료에 도형을 넣으면 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: Putting shapes in a presentation makes it look nice.

explain: 도형은 수학에서 쓰는 말이에요. 삼각형, 사각형, 원 같은 평면 모양이나 정육면체 같은 입체 모양을 모두 포함해요. 일상에서 물건의 모습을 말할 때는 '모양'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 도형 is a math word covering flat shapes like 삼각형, 사각형, and 원, as well as solid shapes like a cube. In everyday life, when you talk about how an object looks, you say 모양 instead.

en: to agree; to share the feeling

examples.en: I agree with that opinion too.

examples.ko: 친구의 말에 깊이 동감해서 고개를 끄덕였어요.
examples.en: I agreed deeply with my friend and nodded.
Many students agreed with that idea.
If you agree, please raise your hand.

examples.ko: 그 기사를 읽고 동감하는 사람이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people who read that article felt the same.
I can't agree completely.

explain: 동감하다는 상대의 생각이나 느낌이 나도 같다고 말할 때 써요. '동의하다'는 제안이나 계획을 받아들이는 쪽이고, 동감하다는 마음이 같다는 쪽이에요. 대화에서는 '저도 그래요'나 '맞아요'가 더 자연스러운 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: 동감하다 is for saying you feel or think the same as the other person. 동의하다 leans toward accepting a proposal or plan, while 동감하다 is about sharing the feeling. In casual talk, 저도 그래요 or 맞아요 often sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 이 제품은 문제가 있어서 리콜이 결정됐어요.
examples.en: A recall was decided for this product because of a problem.
The car company announced that it will recall the cars.
I saw news about a milk recall on TV.

examples.ko: 리콜 대상인지 번호로 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can check by number whether it is subject to the recall.

examples.ko: 이 모델은 리콜 대상이라서 무료로 수리받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: This model is subject to a recall, so you can get it repaired for free.
The store closed because of the recall.

explain: 리콜은 회사가 결함이 있는 제품을 거두어 고치거나 바꿔 주는 거예요. 손님이 마음에 안 들어서 하는 '환불'이나 '교환'과 달라요. 주로 자동차, 식품, 전자제품 뉴스에서 들어요.
explain_en: 리콜 is when a company takes back a defective product to fix or replace it. It is different from 환불 or 교환, which a customer asks for because they are unhappy with an item. You mostly hear it in news about cars, food, and electronics.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에 두 팀의 맞대결이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a head-to-head match between the two teams this evening.

examples.ko: 형과 저는 게임에서 자주 맞대결을 해요.
examples.en: My brother and I often have showdowns in games.
I really want to win this showdown.

examples.ko: 두 가수의 맞대결이 큰 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The face-off between the two singers became a big topic.
I was curious about the result, so I waited all night.
Old rivals face off in the final.

explain: 맞대결은 두 상대가 서로 정면으로 겨루는 거예요. 경기에서 '대결'만 쓰면 일반적인 겨루기이고, '맞'이 붙으면 힘이 비슷한 둘이 직접 마주한다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 '맞대결을 펼치다', '맞대결을 벌이다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 맞대결 is two opponents going straight at each other. Plain 대결 is general competing, but adding 맞 gives more of a feeling that two evenly matched sides face off directly. It usually appears as 맞대결을 펼치다 or 맞대결을 벌이다.

examples.en: My father is a carpenter who has worked for a long time.
A carpenter came and fixed the door.
A famous carpenter made this chair.

examples.ko: 저는 나중에 목수가 되어서 집을 짓고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to become a carpenter and build houses later.
The carpenter is cutting wood.

examples.ko: 한옥을 짓는 목수는 특별한 기술이 필요해요.
examples.en: A carpenter who builds hanok needs special skills.

explain: 목수는 나무로 집이나 가구를 만드는 사람이에요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 '목수님'이라고 해요. 한국어에서 나무를 다루는 일은 '목공'이라고도 하고, '목공 수업', '목공 체험'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 목수 is a person who builds houses or furniture out of wood. When addressing one directly, people usually say 목수님. Working with wood is also called 목공, as in 목공 수업 or 목공 체험.

examples.en: The plenary session is held tomorrow morning.
What the committee decided moved on to the plenary session.

examples.ko: 본회의 전에 작은 회의를 먼저 했어요.
examples.en: We held a small meeting before the plenary session.
The news showed scenes from the plenary session.
All members have to attend the plenary session.
The school representatives gave their opinions at the plenary session.

explain: 본회의는 위원회나 분과 회의가 아니라 구성원 전체가 모이는 정식 회의예요. 작은 모임에서 먼저 의논하고, 마지막에 본회의에서 결정하는 순서가 많아요. 일상에서는 뉴스, 국회, 학회 같은 곳에서 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: 본회의 is the formal full meeting where all members gather, as opposed to a committee or subgroup meeting. A common order is to discuss in small groups first and decide at the 본회의 last. You mostly hear it in the news, in parliament reports, and in academic societies.

examples.ko: 올해는 계속 불운이 따라다니는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It feels like bad luck keeps following me this year.

examples.ko: 비 때문에 경기가 취소된 건 정말 불운이었어요.
examples.en: It was really bad luck that the game was canceled because of the rain.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 부상이라는 불운을 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: That player overcame the misfortune of an injury.
Unlucky things happened all at once.

examples.ko: 저는 불운을 탓하지 않고 다시 도전했어요.
examples.en: I didn't blame bad luck and tried again.

examples.ko: 불운 속에서도 가족이 힘이 되어 줬어요.
examples.en: Even in misfortune, my family gave me strength.

explain: 불운은 운이 나쁜 상태를 점잖게 말하는 글 같은 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '운이 없다', '재수 없다'를 더 많이 써요. 반대말은 '행운'이에요.
explain_en: 불운 is a somewhat formal, written-style word for bad luck. In daily conversation, Koreans more often say 운이 없다 or 재수 없다. Its opposite is 행운.

examples.en: The teacher explained the rules in detail.
Please tell me the details of the accident.
I read the contract carefully before signing.

examples.ko: 여행 일정은 메일로 상세히 보내 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll send the travel schedule in detail by email.

examples.ko: 의사가 약 먹는 방법을 상세히 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me how to take the medicine in detail.
I want to know the results in more detail.

explain: 상세히는 빠짐없이 자세하게 한다는 느낌이에요. 같은 뜻의 '자세히'는 말할 때 훨씬 자연스럽고, 상세히는 설명서, 뉴스, 회사 문서 같은 격식 있는 자리에서 잘 써요. 반대로 간단하게 하는 건 '간단히'나 '대충'이에요.
explain_en: 상세히 gives the feeling of leaving nothing out. 자세히 means the same and is much more natural in speech, while 상세히 fits formal places like manuals, news, and company documents. The opposite is doing it briefly: 간단히 or 대충.

examples.en: When I go to a bookstore, I look at the new releases section first.
A new book by my favorite writer came out today.
I'll check whether new books have come into the library.

examples.ko: 이번 달 신간 중에서 하나를 골랐어요.
examples.en: I picked one from this month's new releases.

examples.ko: 신간은 보통 책값이 조금 더 비싸요.
examples.en: New books are usually a bit more expensive.
I gave my friend a newly published novel as a gift.

explain: 신간은 새로 나온 책이에요. 영화나 음악의 새 작품은 '신작'이라고 해서 책에만 써요. 서점에서는 오래전에 나온 책을 '구간'이라고도 하지만, 일상에서는 '예전에 나온 책'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: 신간 is a newly published book. A new film or album is called '신작', so 신간 is used only for books. Bookstores sometimes call older titles '구간', but in daily speech people say '예전에 나온 책'.

examples.en: The audience shouted for an encore loudly.
The singer sang one last song as an encore.
Even after the show ended, the encore applause continued.
The encore song was better than the main show.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 인기가 많아서 앙코르 상영을 해요.
examples.en: This movie is so popular that they are showing it again.
The encore stage was short but really moving.

explain: 앙코르는 공연이 끝난 뒤 관객이 더 해 달라고 요청하는 거예요. 한국에서는 '앙코르!'라고 외치거나 박수를 계속 치는 방식으로 표현해요. 공연이나 영화를 다시 하는 '앙코르 공연', '앙코르 상영'으로도 써요.
explain_en: 앙코르 is when the audience asks for more after a performance ends. In Korea, people shout 앙코르 or keep clapping to ask for it. It is also used for repeat runs, as in 앙코르 공연 or 앙코르 상영.

examples.en: This place's kimchi stew is the best in the neighborhood.
In our class, Minsu is the best at running.
Health comes first, so don't overdo it.

examples.ko: 으뜸 상품으로 뽑힌 책이 정말 재미있어요.
examples.en: The book chosen as the top item is really fun.
I learned that manners are the top virtue.
That singer's song is counted as the best.

explain: 으뜸은 여럿 가운데 가장 뛰어나거나 가장 중요한 것을 말해요. '최고'와 비슷하지만 으뜸은 순서에서 맨 앞이라는 느낌이 있어서 '으뜸가는', '으뜸이다'처럼 써요. 말할 때보다 글이나 광고에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: 으뜸 means the most excellent or most important among many. It is close to 최고, but 으뜸 carries a feeling of being first in the order, and appears as 으뜸가는 or 으뜸이다. You see it more in writing and ads than in speech.

examples.en: My grandfather farmed in the countryside.
My grandfather taught me Chinese characters.

examples.ko: 조부 댁에 가면 항상 맛있는 밥을 먹어요.
examples.en: When I go to my grandfather's house, I always eat delicious food.
I have to write my grandfather's name on the form.
My grandfather passed away last year.

examples.ko: 거실에 조부께서 쓰신 글씨가 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A piece of calligraphy my grandfather wrote hangs in the living room.

explain: 조부는 아버지의 아버지를 격식 있게 부르는 말이에요. 어머니 쪽 할아버지는 '외조부'라고 해서 구분해요. 평소에는 '할아버지'를 쓰고, 조부는 서류나 어른 앞에서 정중하게 말할 때 써요. 상대방의 할아버지를 높일 때는 '조부님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 조부 is the formal word for one's father's father. The maternal grandfather is called 외조부, which keeps the two apart. In daily life Koreans say 할아버지, and use 조부 on documents or when speaking politely to elders. To honor someone else's grandfather, you say 조부님.

examples.en: Is there a nonstop bus to Seoul?

examples.ko: 직행으로 가면 두 시간밖에 안 걸려요.
examples.en: If you take the express, it takes only two hours.
After work I went straight home.

examples.ko: 직행 열차는 표가 조금 더 비싸요.
examples.en: The express train ticket is a bit more expensive.
A direct shuttle runs from the airport to the hotel.

examples.ko: 이 버스는 직행이라서 중간에 안 서요.
examples.en: This bus is nonstop, so it doesn't stop on the way.

explain: 직행은 중간에 서지 않고 곧장 가는 거예요. 모든 정류장에 서는 버스는 '완행'이라고 하고, 시외버스에서 '직행'과 '완행'을 구분해서 불러요. 멈추지 않고 바로 간다는 뜻으로 '직행하다'처럼 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: 직행 is going straight to the destination without stopping on the way. A bus that stops at every stop is 완행, and intercity buses are labeled either 직행 or 완행. It is also used as a verb, 직행하다, for heading somewhere directly.

examples.en: I like this fabric because its texture is soft.
The painter expressed a rough texture with paint.
The chewy texture of the bread is really good.
You can't feel the texture well in a photo.

examples.ko: 벽지 질감 때문에 방이 따뜻해 보여요.
examples.en: The room looks warm because of the wallpaper texture.

examples.ko: 손으로 만져 보면 질감을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tell the texture by touching it with your hand.

explain: 질감은 손으로 만지거나 눈으로 봤을 때 느껴지는 표면의 느낌이에요. 음식에서는 보통 '식감'이라고 하고, 옷이나 그림, 화장품에서는 질감을 써요. '부드러운 질감', '거친 질감'처럼 형용사와 같이 말해요.
explain_en: 질감 is the feeling of a surface, whether touched or seen. For food, Koreans usually say 식감 instead, and use 질감 for clothes, paintings, and cosmetics. It pairs with adjectives, as in 부드러운 질감 and 거친 질감.

examples.en: An old car has to be scrapped.

examples.ko: 사고가 크게 나서 그 차는 폐차가 됐어요.
examples.en: The accident was big, so that car was scrapped.
I called a scrapping company and asked the price.
After scrapping, you need to handle the insurance.
That car is almost ready to be scrapped.

examples.ko: 폐차장에는 낡은 자동차가 많이 모여 있어요.
examples.en: Many old cars are gathered at the scrapyard.

explain: 폐차는 낡거나 부서진 차를 더 이상 쓰지 않고 없애는 거예요. 차를 파는 '중고차 판매'와 달라서, 도로에서 아예 쓰지 않게 등록을 지워요. 차를 모으는 곳은 '폐차장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 폐차 means getting rid of an old or wrecked car for good. It differs from selling a used car, because the car is deregistered and no longer used on the road. The place where such cars are collected is called a 폐차장.

examples.ko: 십오 년 된 차를 이번 주에 폐차해요.
examples.en: I'm scrapping my fifteen-year-old car this week.
The car was so old that I decided to scrap it.

examples.ko: 사고 난 차를 폐차했는데 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: I scrapped the crashed car and it hurt.

examples.ko: 폐차하면 보조금을 받을 수 있는 경우도 있어요.
examples.en: If you scrap a car, you can sometimes receive a subsidy.
My father is cleaning out the car he is going to scrap.
After scrapping the car, I get around by public transportation.

explain: 폐차하다는 차를 완전히 없앨 때 쓰는 말이에요. 차를 팔 때는 '팔다', 새 차로 바꿀 때는 '바꾸다'를 써서 폐차와 구분해요. '차를 폐차하다'는 같은 말이 겹쳐서 어색하니 그냥 '폐차하다'나 '폐차를 하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: 폐차하다 is used when a car is disposed of for good. When you sell a car you say '팔다', and when you swap to a new one you say '바꾸다', which separates them from 폐차. '차를 폐차하다' repeats the same word and sounds awkward, so people just say '폐차하다' or '폐차를 하다'.

examples.ko: 축구 해설자가 선수들의 움직임을 설명해 줘요.
examples.en: The soccer commentator explains the players' movements.

examples.ko: 저 해설자는 말이 빨라서 이해하기 어려워요.
examples.en: That commentator speaks fast, so it's hard to understand.
A guide at the museum introduced the paintings.

examples.ko: 저는 나중에 야구 해설자가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to become a baseball commentator later.
The match was more fun thanks to the commentator.

examples.ko: 해설자의 목소리가 좋아서 계속 듣게 돼요.
examples.en: The commentator's voice is good, so I keep listening.

explain: 해설자는 경기나 전시, 뉴스를 보는 사람이 이해하기 쉽게 설명해 주는 사람이에요. 경기 상황을 바로 말해 주는 사람은 '캐스터', 이유와 전략을 풀어 주는 사람은 해설자예요. 스포츠 방송에서는 보통 둘이 같이 나와요.
explain_en: 해설자 is a person who explains a match, exhibit, or news so viewers can follow it easily. The person who calls the play-by-play is the 캐스터, while the 해설자 explains the reasons and strategy. In sports broadcasts, the two usually appear together.

examples.en: That country has very strong military power.
The news compared the military power of the two countries.
If military power is weak, it is hard to protect a country.

examples.ko: 군사력에 쓰는 돈이 해마다 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The money spent on military power is growing every year.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 옛날 왕국의 군사력을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, we learned about the military power of an old kingdom.
They say both economic power and military power are important.

explain: 군사력은 나라가 가진 군대와 무기의 힘이에요. '경제력', '정치력'처럼 '-력'이 붙는 말 가운데 하나라서 비슷한 짝으로 같이 외우면 좋아요. '병력'은 군인 수만 가리켜서 군사력보다 좁아요.
explain_en: 군사력 is the strength of a country's army and weapons. It belongs to the family of words ending in -력, like 경제력 and 정치력, so it helps to learn them together. 병력 refers only to the number of soldiers, so it is narrower than 군사력.

examples.en: A honeybee is flying around over the flowers.

examples.ko: 꿀벌 덕분에 우리가 맛있는 꿀을 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Thanks to honeybees, we can eat delicious honey.
When spring comes, honeybees work busily.
My grandfather raises honeybees in the mountains.
Many people are worried because honeybees are decreasing.
The child colored the honeybee drawing yellow.

explain: 꿀벌은 꿀을 모으는 벌이에요. 그냥 '벌'은 쏘는 벌 전체를 가리키는 넓은 말이고, 꿀벌은 그 가운데 꿀을 만드는 종류예요. 부지런히 일하는 사람을 '꿀벌처럼 일한다'고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: 꿀벌 is the bee that gathers honey. Plain 벌 is the broad word for stinging insects of this kind, and 꿀벌 is the type among them that makes honey. Koreans may also say someone works 꿀벌처럼 to praise a diligent worker.

examples.en: At night, moths gathered near the light.
A moth came in through the window.

examples.ko: 나방은 나비보다 색이 어두운 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Moths are often darker in color than butterflies.
I was startled when a moth came out of the closet.
The moth caterpillars ate all the leaves.
I'm scared of moths, so I avoid them.

explain: 나비는 낮에 날고 앉을 때 날개를 접는 경우가 많고, 나방은 밤에 날고 앉을 때 날개를 펴는 경우가 많아요. 밤에 불빛에 모이는 모습 때문에 '불나방'이라는 말도 있는데, 위험한 줄 모르고 뛰어드는 사람을 비유할 때 써요.
explain_en: Butterflies tend to fly by day and fold their wings when they rest, while moths tend to fly at night and keep their wings spread when they rest. Because moths gather around lights at night, there is also the word '불나방', used figuratively for someone who rushes into danger without realizing it.

examples.en: A huge airship is floating in the sky.
In the old days, airships also carried people.
An airship is much slower than an airplane.

examples.ko: 저는 비행선을 타고 여행하는 상상을 해요.
examples.en: I imagine traveling by airship.
The airship ad stood out in the sky.

examples.ko: 만화 속 비행선이 너무 멋있어서 따라 그렸어요.
examples.en: The airship in the cartoon was so cool that I drew it too.

explain: 비행선은 가벼운 기체를 채운 큰 풍선 같은 몸체로 하늘을 나는 탈것이에요. 날개로 나는 '비행기'와 달라서 아주 천천히 움직여요. 요즘에는 타는 일보다 광고나 영화에서 더 자주 봐요.
explain_en: 비행선 is a vehicle with a big balloon-like body filled with lighter-than-air gas. It is different from a 비행기, which flies on wings, and it moves very slowly. These days you see it more in ads and movies than you actually ride one.

en: sabal (large bowl for rice or soup)

examples.ko: 할머니가 사발에 밥을 가득 담아 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother filled a bowl to the brim with rice.
The soup in the bowl is still hot.
The country house has many old bowls.

examples.ko: 설날에 떡국을 큰 사발에 담아 먹었어요.
examples.en: On Lunar New Year's Day we ate rice cake soup from a big bowl.
I poured water into a bowl and gave it to the dog.
The bowl is big, so hold it with two hands.

explain: 밥이나 국을 담는 크고 우묵한 그릇이에요. 보통 쓰는 '밥그릇'보다 크고 옛날식 느낌이 있어서 시골집이나 전통 음식 이야기에서 잘 나와요. '사발면'이라는 라면 이름에도 이 말이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: It is a large, deep dish for rice or soup. It is bigger than an ordinary '밥그릇' and feels old-fashioned, so it often appears in stories about country homes and traditional food. The word is also part of the noodle product name '사발면'.

examples.en: Korea and Vietnam established diplomatic relations in 1992.

examples.ko: 수교 삼십 주년을 기념하는 행사가 열렸어요.
examples.en: An event marking the thirtieth anniversary of diplomatic ties was held.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 수교 이후 교류가 크게 늘었어요.
examples.en: Since establishing relations, exchanges between the two countries have grown a lot.
The number of countries with diplomatic ties grew gradually.
We learned about the process of establishing relations in history class.
Thanks to diplomatic relations, flight routes were also created.

explain: 수교는 나라와 나라가 정식으로 외교 관계를 맺는 거예요. 보통 '수교하다', '수교를 맺다'로 쓰고, 한국과 다른 나라의 사이를 말할 때 '수교 몇 주년'이라고 해요. 관계를 끊는 건 '단교'라고 해요.
explain_en: 수교 is two countries formally starting diplomatic relations. It is usually used as 수교하다 or 수교를 맺다, and anniversaries are called 수교 몇 주년. Cutting those ties is called 단교.

examples.en: This work is also an extension of the last project.

examples.ko: 그 말은 어제 싸움의 연장선에서 나온 거예요.
examples.en: That remark came as a continuation of yesterday's fight.
I opened a small shop as an extension of my hobby.
This book is a continuation of the previous one.
If you think of it as a continuation of study, it's not hard.

examples.ko: 선을 길게 그어서 연장선을 만들어 보세요.
examples.en: Draw the line longer to make an extension line.

explain: 연장선은 원래 선을 더 길게 이은 선인데, 일이나 생각이 앞의 것에서 이어진다는 뜻으로 많이 써요. '~의 연장선에서', '~의 연장선이다'로 자주 말해요. 완전히 새로운 시작을 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: 연장선 is literally a line extended further, but Koreans mostly use it to say that a task or idea continues from something before. It often appears as ~의 연장선에서 or ~의 연장선이다. It is not used for a completely fresh start.

examples.en: I heard an owl in the forest at night.
Owls see well even in dark places.
I saw a big owl for the first time at the zoo.

examples.ko: 저는 밤늦게까지 깨어 있는 올빼미 같은 사람이에요.
examples.en: I'm a night owl who stays up late.
The owl's eyes are big and round, so it's cute.

examples.ko: 아이가 올빼미 모양 가방을 갖고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The child wants an owl-shaped bag.

explain: 올빼미는 밤에 활동하는 새예요. 비슷한 '부엉이'는 머리 위에 귀처럼 보이는 깃털이 있는 쪽을 말하는데, 일상에서는 둘을 섞어서 쓰기도 해요. 사람에게는 '올빼미'를 밤늦게까지 깨어 있는 사람으로 비유해요.
explain_en: 올빼미 is a bird that is active at night. The similar 부엉이 refers to owls with ear-like feather tufts on top of the head, though in daily speech people sometimes mix the two. For people, 올빼미 is used figuratively for someone who stays up late.

examples.en: I climbed a mountain and saw the Milky Way for the first time.

examples.ko: 맑은 날 밤하늘에는 은하수가 선명하게 보여요.
examples.en: On a clear night, the Milky Way is clearly visible in the sky.

examples.ko: 도시에서는 불빛 때문에 은하수가 안 보여요.
examples.en: In the city, you can't see the Milky Way because of the lights.
The children made wishes while looking at the Milky Way.
The photographer went far away to shoot the Milky Way.
Camping under the Milky Way was really romantic.

explain: 은하수는 밤하늘에 하얀 강처럼 길게 보이는 별 무리예요. 이름에 '물 수'가 들어가서 '은빛 강'이라는 느낌이 있고, 옛 이야기인 견우와 직녀가 건너지 못한 강이 바로 은하수예요. 영어와 달리 우유가 아니라 강으로 상상했어요.
explain_en: 은하수 is the long band of stars that looks like a white river across the night sky. The name contains 水, meaning water, giving a "silver river" feeling, and the river that the lovers in the old tale of 견우 and 직녀 could not cross is the 은하수. Unlike English "Milky Way," Koreans imagined a river, not milk.

examples.ko: 부산 지부장이 이번 주에 본사에 와요.
examples.en: The Busan branch manager is coming to headquarters this week.
I sent the report to the branch manager.

examples.ko: 새로 온 지부장은 직원들 이야기를 잘 들어요.
examples.en: The newly arrived branch manager listens well to the staff.
Our association's branch head is chosen by vote.
The branch manager changed, so the atmosphere changed.
My father works as a branch chief at an association.

explain: 지부장은 본부 아래 지역 지부를 이끄는 사람이에요. 은행이나 가게의 '지점장'과 비슷하지만, 지부장은 협회나 노동조합, 단체의 지역 조직에서 더 자주 써요. 부르는 말은 '지부장님'이에요.
explain_en: 지부장 is the person who leads a regional branch under a headquarters. It is similar to 지점장 for a bank or shop, but 지부장 is used more often for regional units of associations, unions, and organizations. The way to address one is 지부장님.

examples.en: The president is in his office right now.
I waited for a moment in front of the office door.
The mayor's office is on the third floor.
The office was full of a big desk and papers.
When guests come, we talk in the office.
The president's office appeared on the news.

explain: 집무실은 높은 직책의 사람이 일하는 방이에요. 일반 직원의 일하는 곳은 '사무실'이라고 하고, 사장이나 시장처럼 책임이 큰 사람의 방일 때 집무실이라고 해요. 보통 '대통령 집무실', '사장 집무실'처럼 직책과 함께 말해요.
explain_en: 집무실 is the room where a high-ranking person works. A regular employee's workplace is a 사무실, while 집무실 is used for the room of someone with big responsibility, like a president or mayor. It usually comes with a title, as in 대통령 집무실 or 사장 집무실.

examples.en: Our house is heated with natural gas.

examples.ko: 천연가스 가격이 올라서 요금이 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The price of natural gas went up, so the bill was high.
This bus runs on natural gas.
Natural gas pollutes the air less than coal.

examples.ko: 한국은 천연가스를 다른 나라에서 많이 사 와요.
examples.en: Korea buys a lot of natural gas from other countries.
The news said the supply of natural gas decreased.

explain: 천연가스는 땅속에서 나오는 불에 타는 기체예요. 집에서 요리하고 난방할 때 쓰는 '도시가스'도 대부분 천연가스로 만들어요. 줄여서 'LNG'라고도 하는데, 이건 액체로 만든 천연가스를 가리켜요.
explain_en: 천연가스 is a flammable gas that comes out of the ground. The 도시가스 used for cooking and heating at home is mostly made from natural gas. It is also abbreviated LNG, which specifically means natural gas turned into liquid.

examples.en: It's really dangerous to climb onto the railroad tracks.
The train passed slowly along the tracks.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 철로 옆이라서 기차 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: My house is next to the tracks, so I hear trains.
Construction to lay new tracks has begun.
A lot of snow fell, so the tracks froze.

examples.ko: 옛날 철로를 산책길로 바꾼 곳이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a place where old tracks were turned into a walking path.

explain: 철로는 기차가 다니는 길, 즉 레일이 놓인 길이에요. 비슷한 '선로'는 철도 용어로 더 많이 쓰고, 철로는 일상에서 길로서의 느낌이 강해요. 둘을 거의 같은 뜻으로 써도 괜찮아요.
explain_en: 철로 is the path on which trains run, meaning the road where rails are laid. The similar 선로 is used more as a railway term, while 철로 feels more like a road in everyday talk. You can use the two with almost the same meaning.

examples.ko: 처음 시작했을 때의 초심을 잊지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't forget the initial resolve you had when you first started.
A person who keeps their original resolve even after success is cool.
Every time it gets hard, I recall my original resolve.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 초심 그대로 팬들을 대해요.
examples.en: That singer treats fans just as in the beginning.
I'll go back to the beginning and practice again.

examples.ko: 오래 일하다 보면 초심이 흐려질 수 있어요.
examples.en: After working for a long time, your original resolve can fade.

explain: 초심은 처음 일을 시작할 때 가졌던 순수하고 진지한 마음이에요. '초심을 잃지 않다', '초심으로 돌아가다'처럼 쓰고, 새해나 입학, 입사 때 많이 말해요. 처음의 서툴고 모르는 상태를 뜻하는 '초보'와는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: 초심 is the pure, earnest attitude you had when you first started something. It appears as 초심을 잃지 않다 or 초심으로 돌아가다, and people say it a lot at New Year, school entry, or a new job. It is different from 초보, which means being a beginner with little skill.

examples.en: The neighborhood bookstore is closing down next month.
Customers decreased, so we decided to close the shop.
Many restaurants closed down during COVID.
I heard the news that the owner is closing down.
After closing the business, I looked for new work.
If you close a business, you must report it to the tax office.

explain: 폐업하다는 가게나 회사가 영업을 완전히 끝낼 때 써요. 잠깐 쉬는 '휴업하다'와 달라서 다시 열지 않는다는 느낌이에요. 문을 열고 새로 시작하는 건 '개업하다'예요.
explain_en: 폐업하다 is used when a shop or company ends its business completely. It differs from 휴업하다, which means closing for a while, because 폐업하다 feels like it will not reopen. Starting a business is 개업하다.
